name: Sprig moulding
summary: A small relief is pressed in a mould of fired clay, lifted out and fixed to the damp body with water. Potters use it to add figures and leaves.
how: Carve the relief in reverse in a small mould of fired clay.
Press a thin piece of soft clay into the mould and trim it flat.
Lift the sprig out with the tip of a knife.
Wet the body and press the sprig on it, then fettle the edge.

origin.note: Staffordshire potters press white clay reliefs into moulds and fix them to the body of salt-glazed stoneware.

adoptions.via: Wedgwood workers press fine white sprigs of classical figures onto the stained jasper body of urns and vases.
